records.found: On 2026-11-06 Nature Aging published (online) a mouse study naming vanadyl sulfate, a mineral supplement, as an aged-cell-clearing drug that extended lifespan in male mice; I read the abstract on Europe PMC, not the full paper. It is an animal result of the kind the record already holds, so it does not move the stage.

findings.what: Nature Aging paper 'Altered protein cysteine reactivity in senescent cells is a vulnerability for senolysis to ameliorate aging': oral vanadyl sulfate cleared aged cells, eased age-related disorders and extended lifespan in male mice.

records.found: The only dated item bearing on the test is the new fisetin trial record (first posted 2026-11-05): a completed randomised trial of 82 people whose main measure is the change in senescent blood immune cells. No results are posted, so it does not meet the test yet, but results could later add a second measurement trial. The Duke COPD record (NCT07275359, updated 2026-11-03) is not yet recruiting and measures blood ageing markers with metformin.

findings.what: The registry posted a new record (first posted 2026-11-05) for a completed randomised trial of fisetin from the Steadman Philippon Research Institute: 82 people, started 2023-05-24, finished 2024-01-30. Its main measure is the change in senescent blood immune cells, a measurement, not a clinical benefit. No results are posted.

records.found: On 2026-10-29 Cell Stem Cell published (online) a mouse study of uPAR-directed CAR T cells in Duchenne muscular dystrophy that removed uPAR-carrying inflammatory and scarring cell subsets; I read the abstract on Europe PMC. It extends uPAR CAR T cells to a new animal condition but is not a person treated and not aged cells as such. Searches found no first-in-human registration.

findings.what: Cell Stem Cell: uPAR-directed CAR T cells remove pathogenic macrophage and fibro-adipogenic progenitor subsets and improve muscle in mouse models of Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
